podcast.title: Apollo 11 Telemetry Use
podcast.body: The album "The Race for Space" by Public Service Broadcasting incorporates various elements, including telemetry and communication snippets between mission control and Apollo 11, to narrate its historical theme. "This piece uses all kinds of telemetry and communication between mission control and Apollo 11."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contemporary Geek Rock Bearer
podcast.body: Public Service Broadcasting was identified as one of today's flag-flyers for Geek Rock, continuing the tradition of bands that incorporate intellectual and technological themes into their music. "Today's flyers of the flag include public service broadcasting, the decemberists, tidus and andronicus and all j."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: London-Based Instrumental Group
podcast.body: Public Service Broadcasting is a four-member group from London recognized for their Post-Progressive sound, which primarily features instrumentals. "four guys from London whose best work features instrumentals with the only vocals being spoken word bits taken from old public information films, archival footage, material in the public domain, and even old propaganda."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spoken Word Vocals from Archival Sources
podcast.body: A unique aspect of Public Service Broadcasting's music is the use of spoken word vocals, which are exclusively sourced from old public information films, archival footage, public domain material, and historical propaganda. "with the only vocals being spoken word bits taken from old public information films, archival footage, material in the public domain, and even old propaganda."

podcast.title: Unique Sampling Technique
podcast.body: This British band creates instrumental music by incorporating samples from old public service announcements and educational films, a method that is explicitly identified as "definitely nerdy." "Public service broadcasting, a British band that uses samples from old public service announcements and educational films over instrumental, they write. Definitely nerdy."
